title: Captains of crush product review
summary: Review of IronMind Captains of Crush grippers. He praises their durability, the fine gradation of levels that makes progression easy, and the thin handles that are more comfortable than padded cheap grippers. He recommends pairing them with hand-extensor elastics to avoid elbow pain and using them during rest periods as a low-fatigue forearm accessory.

claims.claim: Captains of Crush grippers are extremely durable: some of his have lasted 4-5 years without rusting or damage, while cheaper grippers he bought broke.
Because there are many gripper levels, progression is easy: if you can close a #1 about 10 times, you can close the #1.5 a few times.
Grippers are not the best tool to grow forearms, but they are a useful hypertrophy accessory because they are not taxing and can be done between sets without winding you.
Thin gripper handles are more comfortable than padded ones: padding rolls in the hand, and a smaller surface area lets you position the handle on the hand muscle instead of pressing on nerves.
He had hand pain training with previous grippers and has had no issues since switching to Captains of Crush.
The gripper price is reasonable given they last a lifetime; buying them bundled with extensor elastics is usually cheaper.
Too much gripper work alone can cause elbow pain; complementing it with elastic band hand-opening work (the antagonist muscles) prevents this.
A good way to train grip: during the ~3-minute rests between heavy squat sets, do grippers superset with hand-opening elastics.
Gripper work is not very fatiguing, but avoid doing it every day or the day before a pulling session done without straps, since grip needs to be fresh.
The Captains of Crush scale goes to #4; closing the #4 is a massive achievement, and closing the #2.5 or #3 already means a very strong grip.
Beginners should start with the Trainer gripper and buy higher levels only once they can close the current one; don't buy all at once or start too high.
